articles.title: Measurement of Femoral Neck Anteversion Angle in Children With Intoeing Gait by Using Femoral Plain Radiographs: A Retrospective Observational Study.
articles.authors: Liu MY, Yao SH, Liaw CK, Wang JH, Lin CH, Chen CH
articles.population: Children aged 5 to 12 years with intoeing gait
articles.outcomes: Agreement between femoral neck anteversion angle measurements obtained by plain radiography versus CT scan
articles.take_home: Plain radiographs can measure the angle of the thighbone neck just as well as CT scans in children with intoeing gait, with only a tiny difference that does not matter for treatment decisions. This means children can avoid the extra radiation exposure from CT scanning.

articles.title: Success Rate of Distal Radius Epiphysiodesis for Progressive Pediatric Wrist Deformity: A Pilot Study.
articles.authors: Ghetti CB, Ho T, Campbell TR, Bomar JD, Edmonds EW
articles.population: Skeletally immature children with wrist deformity undergoing distal radial epiphysiodesis
articles.outcomes: Success rate of physeal closure, radiographic measurements (ulnar variance, volar tilt, radial inclination), clinical symptoms (pain, strength, instability, range of motion), complication rate
articles.take_home: Distal radial epiphysiodesis successfully achieved bone closure in 93.8% of wrists with wrist deformity in children, with no complications reported. The procedure appears to be a safe treatment option for wrist deformity caused by abnormal bone growth or injury.

articles.title: Beyond Initial Correction: Recurrence Patterns After Ponseti Treatment in 257 Children.
articles.authors: Rajjoub R, Murata A, Slyepkan I, DeVilbiss A, Shobode MA, Wani M, et al.
articles.population: Children with idiopathic clubfoot treated with Ponseti method
articles.outcomes: Recurrence of clubfoot deformity; factors associated with recurrence; outcomes of treatment for recurrent deformity; association between tibialis anterior tendon transfer and repeat recurrence
articles.take_home: More than half of children treated for clubfoot had recurrence of the deformity, and poor adherence to bracing was the strongest risk factor for this. When recurrence happened, surgery including tendon transfer gave better long-term results than casting alone, which often led to further recurrence.

articles.title: Tips and tricks for femoral Fassier-Duval rod revision in osteogenesis imperfecta.
articles.population: Patients with osteogenesis imperfecta undergoing femoral Fassier-Duval rod revision surgery
articles.sample_size: 76 limbs from 37 patients; 21 femoral revisions analysed in detail; 10 limbs from 9 patients reviewed for technical strategies
articles.outcomes: Bone union rates, postoperative complications, rod survival rates, time to union, need for re-revision surgery
articles.take_home: In patients with osteogenesis imperfecta undergoing femoral rod revision, careful surgical planning and technique achieved bone union in 89.5% of cases and 85% rod survival at two years follow-up. However, nearly one in three limbs experienced complications, with 14% requiring further revision surgery.

articles.title: Forty-Two Cases of Pediatric Giant Cell Tumor of Bone: Insights From a 25-Year Multi-Institutional Cohort.
articles.authors: Werenski JO, Connolly JJ, Pandey SR, Gonzalez MR, Heidkamp M, Gebhardt MC, et al.
articles.population: Children and young people under 19 years with giant cell tumour of bone treated surgically
articles.outcomes: Local recurrence rates, recurrence-free survival at 12, 24 and 60 months, association between bone marrow oedema on MRI and recurrence
articles.take_home: Giant cell tumours of bone in young people have high recurrence rates of 45% overall, with tumours showing bone marrow oedema on MRI scans being more likely to recur. Patients with open growth plates had numerically higher recurrence rates than those with closed growth plates, though this difference was not statistically significant.

articles.title: Clinical and radiographic features of fractures raising suspicion of non-accidental trauma in young children: A retrospective emergency department study.
articles.authors: Kocyigit IA, Goymen IM, Yuksel B, Yilmaz G, Aksoy MC
articles.population: Children aged 0-6 years presenting to a tertiary paediatric emergency department
articles.sample_size: 649 children (277 with fractures, 38 classified as possible abuse)
articles.outcomes: Classification of fractures by specificity for non-accidental trauma; age comparison; notification and protective-care placement rates
articles.take_home: Younger children (median 18.5 months) with certain types of fractures, particularly metaphyseal corner and transphyseal lesions, had patterns raising suspicion of non-accidental trauma. However, no abuse notifications or protective-care placements were made despite concerning fracture patterns, suggesting a need for improved standardised assessment and child-protection pathways.

articles.title: Association between serum vitamin D levels and pediatric distal radius fractures: a case-control study.
articles.authors: Gerami MH, Nasr A, Alaei S, Rajabi AH, Toofani S, Heidari SH, et al.
articles.population: Children with distal radius fractures compared to children attending orthopedic clinic for routine checks or minor muscular pain
articles.outcomes: Serum vitamin D, phosphorus, and calcium levels; association with fracture incidence
articles.take_home: This study found no link between vitamin D levels and distal radius fractures in children, even though most children had low vitamin D. This suggests other factors beyond vitamin D may be more important for fracture risk.

articles.title: Adverse events in paediatric spinal deformity surgery - 12-year review of specialist spinal deformity practice.
articles.authors: Bayley EJ, Srinivas S, Bellamy M, Ranjan A, Luttrell DM, Athanassacopoulos M, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective review of prospectively collected data
articles.population: Children and adolescents undergoing surgery for spinal deformity, including adolescent idiopathic scoliosis and other causes
articles.sample_size: 871 patients undergoing 1,020 operations between January 2010 and December 2022
articles.outcomes: Incidence and severity of adverse events after spinal deformity surgery, classified by type (implant-related, infection-related, neurological) and severity using Clavien-Dindo grading
articles.take_home: Over one-third of children having spinal deformity surgery experienced an adverse event, but most were minor and needed little or no further treatment. Implant problems were the most common issue, whilst serious complications like cord injury and death remained rare.

articles.title: Beyond the First Fix: Unraveling the Long-term Impact of Surgical Fixation for Early-onset Slipped Capital Femoral Epiphysis in Children Aged 10 and Younger.
articles.authors: Liu DS, Batty M, Cohen L, Morcos M, Wan N, De Silva S, et al.
articles.population: Children aged 10 years or younger with slipped capital femoral epiphysis
articles.sample_size: 82 children (77 with unilateral SCFE, 5 with bilateral SCFE)
articles.outcomes: Femoral neck length, arthrochanteric distance, alpha-angle, rates of contralateral SCFE development, need for additional surgery
articles.take_home: In very young children with SCFE, the affected hip develops some structural changes but the other hip usually stays normal whether it has preventive surgery or careful monitoring. Since 73% of monitored hips remained normal, preventive surgery on the other side may not always be necessary in this age group.

articles.title: Open Reduction for Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip in the Newborn Hip Screening Era: Changing Patient Characteristics and Surgical Strategies Without Compromising Outcomes.
articles.authors: Bekmez S, Evren AT, Erdem E, Turhan Y, Sen K, Demir P, et al.
articles.population: Children with developmental dysplasia of the hip who underwent open reduction surgery, divided into screened patients with failed non-operative treatment and neglected patients
articles.outcomes: Radiological outcomes (Severin grade, McKay score), revision surgery rates, complications, proximal femur growth disturbance, need for pelvic osteotomy
articles.take_home: Newborn hip screening with ultrasound led to earlier detection and less extensive surgery, but children who still needed open reduction surgery had equally good long-term results whether they were screened early or presented late. Screening allowed surgeons to do simpler operations without affecting how well children's hips worked afterwards.

articles.title: The Effect of Metabolic Control of Rickets on Deformity Correction Following Hemiepiphysiodesis in Children With X-linked Hypophosphatemic Rickets.
articles.authors: Ryabets-Lienhard A, Marpuri I, Vu MH, Yu VX, Chen I, Grimbly C, et al.
articles.population: Children with X-linked hypophosphatemic rickets undergoing hemiepiphysiodesis for lower limb deformity
articles.outcomes: Angular deformity correction measured by mechanical axis deviation (MAD) at 2 years post-operatively; relationship between metabolic control (serum alkaline phosphatase) and correction rates
articles.take_home: Better control of rickets after surgery, shown by lower alkaline phosphatase levels, was associated with better and faster straightening of leg deformities in children with X-linked hypophosphatemic rickets. This suggests that good medical management of the underlying rickets helps surgical results.

articles.title: Principles or Resources? Best Management of Pediatric Femoral Neck Fractures.
articles.authors: Kim CL, Sarkar S, Vergara ADN, Arkader A
articles.population: Children under 18 years old with pediatric femoral neck fractures
articles.sample_size: 74 fractures in 73 children (39 from US tertiary centre, 35 from Latin American trauma hospital)
articles.outcomes: Complication rates including avascular necrosis (AVN), surgical timing, treatment methods and outcomes
articles.take_home: Treatment principles appear to matter more than resources for managing children's femoral neck fractures, as two hospitals with very different resources achieved similar complication rates and AVN incidence despite differences in how quickly they operated and what surgical techniques they used.

articles.title: Readability and Content Integrity of Discharge Documents for Common Pediatric Orthopaedic Procedures Before and After Artificial Intelligence Simplification.
articles.authors: A Prempeh AG, Saeed R, Hill C, Kopp L, Tenfelde A
articles.study_type: Quality improvement study with content analysis
articles.population: Caregiver-facing discharge documents for paediatric orthopaedic surgical patients
articles.outcomes: Readability grade level, safety-critical errors, completeness gaps, factual accuracy
articles.take_home: Artificial intelligence successfully simplified discharge documents from grade 8.91 to grade 4.97 reading level, making 73% meet recommended standards, but introduced safety-critical errors in 80% of documents that require clinician review before patient use.

articles.title: Outcomes Related to the Use of Standard-Standard versus Standard-Offset Magnetically Controlled Growing Rods.
articles.authors: Blanchard S, Coleman TA, Jordan J, Floccari L, Pahys J, Sarkar S, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective analysis of prospective registry data
articles.population: Children with early-onset scoliosis undergoing bilateral magnetically controlled growing rod surgery
articles.outcomes: Lengthening achieved at first visit, 2 years and 5 years post-surgery; complication rates
articles.take_home: Both rod orientations achieved similar spinal lengthening and had similar complication rates over 5 years. The choice between standard-standard and standard-offset rod orientations does not appear to affect clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Knee Bone Age Estimation Using Capping Interval Index on MRI: Development and Validation of a Quantitative Method.
articles.authors: Lee W, Song KI, Yu SY, Cho YJ, Song MH, Cho TJ, et al.
articles.study_type: Diagnostic method development and validation study
articles.population: Children and young people aged 18 years or younger without conditions affecting knee anatomy or maturation
articles.sample_size: 695 participants (417 in modelling group, 278 in validation group)
articles.outcomes: Accuracy of knee bone age estimation using capping interval index on MRI; correlation between estimated and chronological age
articles.take_home: A new simple method using MRI measurements of the knee can accurately estimate bone age in children, with estimated age matching actual age very closely in testing. This approach could be useful for assessing skeletal maturity in lower-limb conditions in young people.

articles.title: Perspectives of Orthopaedic Trauma Association Members on Firearm Injury Prevention: Results from a 2025 Membership Survey.
articles.sample_size: 503 respondents (13.5% response rate from 3,721 active members)
articles.outcomes: Perspectives on firearm ownership, injury prevention priorities, and support for organisational advocacy; 95.6% of clinically active respondents reported treating firearm-related injuries; 85.3% supported OTA-led prevention advocacy
articles.take_home: Orthopaedic trauma surgeons who treat firearm injuries strongly support non-partisan advocacy efforts to prevent these injuries, with most endorsing firearm safety training, secure storage, and mental health integration as key prevention strategies.
